transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 min
Location: Zoom
Record: yes
Notes: partner technical integration for marketplace listing, runbook, and orchestration fallbacks

Auto-Summary (AI): Discussed marketplace listing prerequisites, required runbook steps for onramp, helm chart packaging, VPC/KMS integration, canary/rollback orchestration, telemetry hooks for Redwood Console, and next steps to provision a test VPC and run a quant/latency lab.

Topics: [runbook, helm, vpc peering, kms, canary rollouts, telemetry, billing meter, onprem connector]

Transcript: (timestamps approx every 30-60s; transcription may contain minor errors)

[00:00:03] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Quick roll call?
[00:00:10] Liam O'Connor: Liam here, CTO at Sable.
[00:00:12] Priya Nair: Priya, Platform lead.
[00:00:15] Daniel Park: Daniel, DevOps.
[00:00:17] Sara Holt: Sara, Security ops.
[00:00:20] Diego Alvarez: Diego, SE, Redwood. I'll take the technical walkthrough.
[00:00:26] Maya Chen: Cool. Goal for today: get alignment on the listing runbook steps, what needs to be in the helm packaging, the VPC/KMS integration for marketplace listing, and the orchestration fallback patterns if dedicated capacity is saturated. Also agree next steps.

[00:01:05] Diego Alvarez: I'll start with an overview — high level for the runbook we recommend these phases: pre-onboard checks, network peering and IAM, helm packaging and chart values, canary deploy + traffic split, telemetry and alerting hooks, and final gating for listing cert. We have a template runbook, link shared in the chat — https://redwood.ai/syncs/sable-runbook-draft (note: internal link).

[00:01:40] Priya Nair: Quick q — for network, do you need VPC peering or a VPC endpoint? We have strict egress rules.
[00:01:55] Diego Alvarez: Either works, both patterns supported. For Marketplace listing we usually prefer a peering because it keeps egress minimal and simplifies metrics backhaul. If you need endpoint-only (private endpoints), we can adapt but need to update the helm values for the S3-like object store and the telemetry sink.

[00:02:20] Daniel Park: Our infra team prefers endpoints for security reasons, less routing. Any known limitations?
[00:02:30] Diego Alvarez: Endpoint pattern is fine, main caveat is if you use private endpoints you need to ensure DNS resolution inside the cluster maps the marketplace control plane hostnames to the endpoints. We sometimes see customers misconfigure split-horizon DNS — leads to KMS calls going out incorrectly.

[00:03:05] Sara Holt: Speaking of KMS — what exactly does Redwood expect for KMS? We run a vault-based HSM wrapper and want to ensure the marketplace listing doesn't require plaintext key export.
[00:03:20] Ravi Gupta: Important note — Redwood supports both cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and customer-managed HSM/Vault. For listing we need to see an envelope encryption flow diagram and confirmation that keys are non-exportable. The runbook has the KMS diagram checklist.

[00:03:50] Liam O'Connor: Ok, we'll share our envelope flow. Do you need a proof of integration or just the diagram for initial gating?
[00:03:58] Diego Alvarez: For initial gating, diagram + short attestation is fine. For final listing we ask for a test where we perform a key-wrapped encrypt/decrypt in the test environment — not with production data. That keeps it low risk.

[00:04:25] Priya Nair: On helm — what files and values should be present? We have an internal CI that packages charts, but you're asking for specific hooks?
[00:04:38] Diego Alvarez: Yes, a few specifics: values for networkPolicy, podSecurityContext, a values schema for KMS endpoint and TLS options, readiness/liveness probes for the runtime, and a canaryTraffic annotation that Redwood's operator reads to orchestrate canary percentages. Also a sample values.yaml for marketplace listing. We'll attach the helm checklist.

[00:05:12] Maya Chen: I'll attach the helm checklist to the runbook draft when I send it.

[00:05:22] Daniel Park: Can you explain that canaryTraffic annotation — is that handled by Redwood operator or do we need a controller?
[00:05:34] Diego Alvarez: Redwood's marketplace operator can perform traffic splits via ingress annotations for supported ingresses (we support nginx, istio, and alb now), but if you use a custom controller we'll provide the manifest hooks. The operator expects a canary annotation like redwood.io/canary-percent: "20" and a control endpoint to flip it. If you prefer, you can implement traffic-split on your side and Redwood will call your endpoint to change weights as part of rollout automation.

[00:06:10] Priya Nair: Good. What about metrics and telemetry — what do you want in the chart?
[00:06:18] Diego Alvarez: Two things: 1) Prometheus metrics endpoint with standard labels: model_id, model_version, route, and 2) a trace hook for distributed tracing — we accept OTLP, Jaeger formats. The Redwood Console will scrape the Prom endpoint and ingest traces if the OTLP exporter is enabled. Also include counters for cache hits/misses (k-v cash in our notes, sorry — kv cache).

[00:06:55] Sara Holt: Will telemetry send any PII? We need to know retention and sampling.
[00:07:02] Ravi Gupta: Telemetry is tokenized; request content is not sent to the hosted telemetry by default — only metadata and hashed prompt signatures for quality monitoring. Retention defaults are 90 days unless you enable extended retention as an add-on. We'll note that in the runbook.

[00:07:35] Liam O'Connor: On fallback patterns — can you walk through the orchestration when dedicated capacity is saturated? We need graceful degradation without failing user-facing requests.

[00:07:50] Diego Alvarez: Sure. Primary pattern: Smart routing -> if dedicated pool is full, requests route to compatible hosted variant with a cost/latency tag. Steps we recommend in runbook: detect saturation via metrics threshold (e.g., queue depth > X for 30s), trigger async traffic shift (canary to hosted 10% then 100%), and flag a quality monitor to compare outputs. The runbook contains automation webhooks and a sample policy.

[00:08:35] Maya Chen: Note — customers often worry about prompt latency differences. We'll include recommended prompt trimming and quantization profiles for the hosted variant to match quality.

[00:08:55] Priya Nair: Quantization — we plan to run 8-bit on our edge. Does Redwood require model artifacts in a particular format?

[00:09:05] Diego Alvarez: We accept standard model bundles (HF-style) and have tooling to convert to our optimized runtime format. For quantized artifacts, provide model + quant metadata and a small test harness. If you plan on on-prem quantized runtime, we'll run a compatibility check in the lab.

[00:09:35] Daniel Park: About billing — as a marketplace listing, how does metering work for Dedicated vs Hosted fallbacks?

[00:09:45] Ravi Gupta: Billing is handled by the marketplace metering connector. For Dedicated, it's commit-based; for hosted fallback it's usage-based. The runbook needs to include a mapping table that indicates which sku to meter when a fallback happens — otherwise carriers or marketplace backends won't reconcile.

[00:10:20] Liam O'Connor: Ok, we'll need that sku mapping; our finance person will want it.

[00:10:30] Maya Chen: We'll add a sample SKU map to the draft.

[00:10:40] Priya Nair: Anything special for on-prem or airgapped deployments? We might have use-cases for airgapped environments.

[00:10:50] Diego Alvarez: For airgapped installs we provide an onprem bundle and an offline installer. Key points in the runbook: checksum verification, offline license binding step, and a sync plan for model updates (we do signed model artifacts). Also need an ops runbook for fallback to local model variants — since there's no hosted fallback in airgapped you need a local smaller variant pre-staged.

[00:11:30] Priya Nair: Good call. We'll flag that internal requirement.

[00:11:45] Sara Holt: Back to security — audit logs and SSO. For listing we need a description of RBAC model, SAML SSO integration points, and audit log retention.

[00:11:58] Ravi Gupta: We support SAML SSO and OIDC. The runbook asks for an example SAML metadata file, an RBAC matrix that maps roles to actions (deploy, rollback, view metrics), and confirmation of audit log pipeline (we can push logs to your syslog or cloud logging via a sink). Default audit retention is 365 days for enterprise customers but marketplace listing requires at least 90 days visible.

[00:12:35] Daniel Park: For the KMS-attested test, do you need us to rotate keys? Our key rotation window is 90 days currently.

[00:12:44] Diego Alvarez: Rotation is fine. For the test we'll just verify the KMS envelope operations succeed; rotation policy does not block listing. For the final marketplace validation we do a short exercise to show key unwrap works during a simulated model update.

[00:13:10] Priya Nair: Will Redwood require network breakpoints in the chart for troubleshooting?

[00:13:20] Diego Alvarez: We recommend optional debug sidecar injection in the values.yaml (enabled: false by default) which you can flip during triage. Also a debug-mode that enables verbose logs for 10 minutes then auto reverts. We'll provide sample manifests.

[00:13:50] Liam O'Connor: Great. On the runbook gating — what's the acceptance criteria for "ready for listing"?

[00:14:00] Diego Alvarez: Checklist: successful VPC connectivity test, KMS envelope test, helm packaging validated (lint + install in test cluster), canary rollout exercise with rollback executed, telemetry hooks verified, and compliance packet uploaded. At that point Marketplace Ops will run a final cert which usually takes 3 business days.

[00:14:30] Maya Chen: We'll put that as the final gate in the runbook doc.

[00:14:45] Priya Nair: Any special logs or traces Redwood needs during the canary? We want to know what to expose.

[00:14:55] Diego Alvarez: Trace spans should include model execution time, kv-cache hit, tokenization time. Instrumentation keys for spans go into the values under telemetry.otlp.endpoint. We'll provide a sample OTLP config.

[00:15:30] Daniel Park: A little worried about performance — can we run a mini benchmark before the listing cert?

[00:15:40] Diego Alvarez: Yes, that's standard. We'll run a small throughput and latency benchmark in your test account. For initial bench we'll target 500 RPS with a 1-2k token mix to simulate production; if that looks good we'll scale to 1k RPS next week.

[00:16:05] Liam O'Connor: Who runs the bench? You or us?

[00:16:10] Diego Alvarez: Redwood SE runs the bench if you give us a perf test namespace and credentials. Diego: takes ownership.

[00:16:20] Priya Nair: About the test account — we need to scrub any PII data; bench will use synthetic prompts.

[00:16:28] Ravi Gupta: That's fine; tests are synthetic and we have a sanitized prompts harness.

[00:16:40] Sara Holt: A couple of compliance Qs: do you capture raw prompts in logs by default?

[00:16:48] Diego Alvarez: No. By default we hash prompt fingerprints for quality regression monitoring. Raw prompts can be captured if you opt in for debug, but that's controlled by an explicit runbook step and requires additional guardrails and a short retention.

[00:17:10] Maya Chen: OK, switching to orchestration fail-safes — we recommend a two-stage fallback: immediate local fallback to a small model variant (if available) and then asynchronous routing to hosted. This reduces user-visible latency spikes.

[00:17:30] Priya Nair: We like that pattern. We'll pre-stage a small variant (distil style) for local fallback.

[00:17:40] Diego Alvarez: Perfect. The runbook will include the commands to seed the local variant and a small cron job to verify it's warmed. Also guidance to keep KV cache cold-start minimal.

[00:18:05] Daniel Park: How do you verify model parity when you fallback to a hosted variant? We need output quality checks.

[00:18:15] Ravi Gupta: We'll run a sample prompt set during canary and compute similarity metrics (BLEU-ish, embedding distance) against the primary model. If deviation exceeds threshold, we'll auto-roll back and notify both teams. We'll include threshold numbers in the runbook but they can be tuned.

[00:18:50] Liam O'Connor: Those thresholds — default values?

[00:18:55] Diego Alvarez: Default embedding cosine threshold 0.92; mean token-level divergence threshold 0.12. We'll put those in the runbook with examples.

[00:19:20] Priya Nair: Where does the canary logic live? In your operator?

[00:19:28] Diego Alvarez: Yes, operator + a webhook. For more complex policies you can host a policy engine and Redwood will call the policy endpoint.

[00:19:50] Maya Chen: Let's talk timeline — what's realistic for Sable to get to listing-ready if you start next week?

[00:19:58] Diego Alvarez: Assuming runbook draft completed this week and you provision a test VPC, typical timeline: 2 weeks for helm packaging and KMS attestation, 1 week for benching and canary exercise, then final cert — so about 4 weeks end-to-end.

[00:20:20] Liam O'Connor: That aligns with our Q3 launch goals.

[00:20:30] Sara Holt: Anything else for marketplace security gating? Network ACLs, hypervisors?

[00:20:38] Ravi Gupta: Marketplace Ops will check for open management ports on nodes, ensure secrets are not in plain text in charts, and verify image provenance (signed images). We'll include a preflight scanner hook in the runbook.

[00:21:00] Daniel Park: Sounds comprehensive. On the image signing — we use cosign. Is that ok?

[00:21:08] Diego Alvarez: cosign is supported. Add signature verification step to CI and include the public key in the runbook.

[00:21:25] Priya Nair: You mentioned runbook templates. Will the draft include an example CI pipeline snippet?

[00:21:33] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include a sample pipeline showing helm lint, cosign verify, and a canary promotion job.

[00:21:45] Liam O'Connor: For the bench results, what metric will you publish back to us? Percentile latencies and success ratios?

[00:21:55] Diego Alvarez: We'll publish p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, error rate, and KV cache efficiency. We'll also capture GPU utilization and token/sec counters.

[00:22:10] Daniel Park: Good. We need to understand memory usage for quantized models.

[00:22:18] Diego Alvarez: We'll surface estimated memory per replica in the bench report and recommended node sizing.

[00:22:30] Priya Nair: Any special requirements for canary rollback time? We need deterministic behavior in our incident runbooks.

[00:22:38] Diego Alvarez: The canary rollback should be < 2 minutes from detection to fully reverted traffic. The operator enforces that if the rollback job is configured with immediate cutover flag. We'll put sample job manifest.

[00:22:55] Sara Holt: Okay. Let's capture dependencies — who from Redwood will be hands-on?

[00:23:02] Maya Chen: Diego will lead technical, Ravi will support security/KMS, and I will coordinate the listing ops and pricing/sku mapping.

[00:23:15] Liam O'Connor: And from Sable — Priya and Daniel will lead implementation, Sara will handle security docs.

[00:23:25] Diego Alvarez: One more note: during bench we may surface tuning recommendations (batch size, kv cache warm window). We'll include recommended quant profiles if you plan to use 8-bit.

[00:23:40] Priya Nair: Makes sense. Any gotchas from other customers?

[00:23:46] Diego Alvarez: Common gotchas: 1) DNS split-horizon misconfig for endpoints, 2) forgetting to set the telemetry OTLP endpoint and then no traces show up, 3) image signature mis-match in CI, and 4) SKU mapping missing causing billing mismatch. We'll highlight those in runbook.

[00:24:15] Liam O'Connor: Great. Let's list immediate next steps again and owners.

[00:24:22] Maya Chen: Summarizing: Maya - send runbook + helm checklist by Monday 2026-06-21; Priya - share VPC peering/endpoint details and a test namespace by 2026-06-22; Diego - schedule bench and run initial 500 RPS by 2026-06-24; Sara - send SOC2 excerpts and KMS diagram by 2026-06-25.

[00:24:55] Priya Nair: We'll aim for those dates.

[00:25:05] Daniel Park: Question — will the runbook include rollback playbook for operators on call?

[00:25:12] Diego Alvarez: Yes, step-by-step rollback, with kubectl commands, operator webhook URL, and a sample incident runbook with escalation contacts.

[00:25:32] Liam O'Connor: Are there any legal or procurement items for marketplace listing?

[00:25:40] Maya Chen: Procurement will need the final SKU map and the contract addendum; we can loop in marketplace contracts team once the technical gates are passed.

[00:25:55] Priya Nair: Ok — please cc our procurement when you have the SKU map.

[00:26:02] Maya Chen: Will do.

[00:26:10] Diego Alvarez: Final minor item: if you plan to support multi-region failover, we need region-specific model artifacts and a replication plan. That increases listing time by ~1 week but we can scope it separately.

[00:26:30] Liam O'Connor: We might add that later. For now one region is fine.

[00:26:40] Priya Nair: Anything else from Sable?

[00:26:45] Sara Holt: Not from security beyond what we covered.

[00:26:50] Daniel Park: No other tech questions.

[00:26:55] Maya Chen: Cool. We'll follow up with the runbook draft and the helm checklist. Diego, do you want to take the bench scheduling?

[00:27:05] Diego Alvarez: Yes I'll send a calendar invite for the bench window and the lab access instructions.

[00:27:12] Maya Chen: Great. Any final clarifications?

[00:27:18] Priya Nair: One small ask — add an example of the canary traffic annotation in the runbook so our CI can set it automatically.

[00:27:25] Diego Alvarez: Noted, will include. Example: redwood.io/canary-percent: "10" and redwood.io/canary-cutover: "false".

[00:27:40] Maya Chen: Alright team — thanks. We'll recap in an email with attachments and next steps.

[00:27:48] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all.

[00:27:50] Priya Nair: Thanks.

[00:27:52] Diego Alvarez: Thanks.

[00:28:00] End of recording (meeting continued offline for 14 min of triage)

Notes: meeting lasted 42 minutes including a 14-minute offline triage recorded context. Some transcription errors (k-v cash for kv cache, K M S spelled out in a couple places). Shared artifacts referenced: runbook draft link (internal), helm checklist attachment, sample OTLP config.
